Aisha Rahman was suspended. Graham Holt wrote his seventh handover note: “it is recommended that the file be closed promptly.”
A new charge was added to Garrett’s file. A thank-you note came to the branch from the file intake unit.
Graham Holt was arrested for murder and bribery. The six closed files were reopened; in two the wrong person had walked free, and in one an innocent person was released.
Malcolm Reeve’s death was closed as suicide. The internal review into him concluded with the note “took his own life, admitting his guilt”.

On 11 May 2029 at 05.40 in Rotherhithe, a man’s body was found on the quay stones beneath the old railway footbridge over Cutter’s Basin. The bridge deck is nine metres above the quay. Found by a local resident on a morning run.

Deceased: Malcolm Reeve (58), district liaison chief. His car is parked beside the bridge’s east stairs. His phone was not found on him.

Patrol note: “An internal review into him has been under way since April (Tanner Lane handover letter). He was under pressure. High likelihood he jumped.”

File intake unit handover note, 11 May 07.30: “Suspicious death. Findings are consistent with suicide. It is recommended that the file be closed promptly by routine procedure.” Signed: file intake chief.

Bermondsey, 11 May 2029.

· In the garage, partly burnt papers in a metal bin: a piece of brown envelope, handwritten “…RA — PERS…”; half of a list of six file numbers.
· In the tool drawer, a switched-off mobile phone with a smashed screen. The serial number matches Malcolm Reeve’s line.
· In the car boot, a long steel-bodied torch. Hair and blood on the end of the body; sent for examination.

Graham Holt was present during the search.
SEARCH RECORD — GRAHAM HOLT’S HOUSE AND GARAGE

The scene plan showed that the stair tower blocked the view of the witness who said “he jumped”; the warehouse camera showed a second man. Reeve’s draft letter and the post log revealed that the envelope stayed with Holt, and the document log that the six handover letters were born on his account. The switchboard log tied the message to Holt’s account and to the bridge; the location record and the search record closed the night.
The apparent sender of a message is not its real sender: ask for the record itself, the session and the place. And look at how the file reached you too — a handover note is also a witness.
Rotherhithe and the bube London branch — 2023–2029

For six years, file intake chief Graham Holt drafted handover letters for money and had district liaison chief Malcolm Reeve sign them as “routine”; Tanner Lane was one of them. Cornered by the internal review, Reeve wrote the truth to Bora and posted it to the branch. Holt received the envelope. On the night of 10 May he sent a message through the branch switchboard’s gateway in the name of Bora’s extension, called Reeve to the bridge, struck him on the back of the head with a torch and pushed him over the railing. The next morning he also wrote the handover note for the file that took over Reeve’s death. The money came from a company in Berlin.
Who is responsible for Malcolm Reeve’s death?
